newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Nat. Grid profits rise, costs eyed.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Nat. Grid profits rise, costs eyed.

text.p: Britain's electricity transmission network National Grid Group Plc should show an underlying rise in year profits when it reports on June 3 and analysts will look for further details on planned cost cuts.
"Their price review is now out of the way so they can focus on stripping out costs and there could be some provisions," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Year pre-tax profits are expected to be between 577 and 597 million stg with a total dividend payout of 11.13 pence per share.
National Grid agreed last October to revised transmission pricing proposed by industry watchdog Offer that included a one-off reduction of 20 percent in the first year starting April 1, 1997.

It said in November that it planned to cut 750 jobs over the next four years as part of a cost-reduction programme and revealed a plan to cut its controllable cost base by around six percent a year in real terms.
"We will be looking for National Grid to reaffirm that six percent cut, with weighting towards the early years," said another analyst.
Analysts will also be looking for an update on its telecommunications subsidiary Energis.
Energis said in January that National Grid might sell a stake in the company, possibly going below 50 percent for one or more strategic investors, this summer.
"It would be nice to know if there is any solution to the Energis ownership question," the analyst said.
National Grid's overseas operations will also be under scrutiny, analysts said.

The company is suing Pakistan's government for cancelling an overhead power lines project, while confusion reigns over a contract in Kazakhstan which National Grid failed to secure despite being told it had exclusive rights to negotiate.
"It's on, off, on, off in the overseas business. We would really like to know where it's going," the analyst said.
